en.headline: Chow Sang Sang detects unauthorised system access with customer and staff data possibly extracted
en.dek: The jeweller said it first identified the incident on 9 November and has reported it to the Privacy Commissioner and police.
body: Chow Sang Sang Holdings International Limited said it recently detected unauthorised access to its systems, first identified on 9 November 2026. Preliminary investigation shows that the affected systems include the group's membership system and official e-commerce channels.

While the investigation continues, some customer and staff data, including personal data, has been accessed without authorisation and may have been extracted, subject to further verification. The group has taken steps to stop all unauthorised access, strengthen system security and engage cybersecurity experts to investigate and advise on appropriate measures.

As at the date of the announcement, the group has reported the incident to the Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data and the Hong Kong Police Force, and is notifying potentially affected customers and staff. The group will continue to monitor developments, co-operate with the authorities and take appropriate steps to investigate, remediate and mitigate any potential impact.
The company noted that the information is based on management's preliminary assessment of currently available information.

zh.headline: 周生生發現系統遭未授權存取 部分客戶及員工資料或曾被提取
zh.dek: 珠寶集團表示11月9日首次識別事件，已向私隱專員公署及警方通報，並正通知可能受影響人士。
body: 周生生集團國際有限公司表示，近日發現系統遭受未經授權存取，本周一首次識別有關事件。初步調查顯示，受影響系統包括集團的會員系統及官方電子商貿渠道。
調查仍在進行中，部分客戶及員工資料（包括個人資料）在未經授權下被存取，並可能已被提取，有待進一步核實。集團已採取措施遏止所有未經授權存取行為、加強系統安全性，並委聘網絡安全專家展開調查及就適當措施提供建議。
截至公告日期，集團已向個人資料私隱專員公署及香港警務處報告事件，並正通知可能受影響的客戶及員工。集團將繼續監察事態發展，與當局合作，並採取適當步驟調查、補救及減輕任何潛在影響。
公司指出，有關資料基於管理層對目前可得資料的初步評估。
